title: Read-only MODFLOW/XMI prepared-solve state forensics for persistent path memory

current_iterate_related.interpretation: XTEMP differs consistently with the distinct current iterate and is not treated as an independent memory carrier by this result.

npf.interpretation: SAT is observable package-state difference consistent with the different current head; G21C does not claim it independently causes the path effect.

bookkeeping.reason: FRESH and HISTORY intentionally have different solve-call histories.

source_semantics.source_observation: NumericalSolution allocates persistent WSAVE/HCHOLD/DEOLD for NONMETH=3 and updates them from previous nonlinear-iteration changes; G21C only reads these memory-manager values.

bounded_conclusions: The persistent G21B call-12 head offset is reproduced exactly under the G21C forensic run.
Accepted XOLD, the frozen outer-2 API HCOF/RHS values and the relevant solver configuration are identical between FRESH and HISTORY, so those quantities do not explain the observed arm difference.

At call 12, explicit delta-bar-delta solver-history carriers WSAVE, HCHOLD and DEOLD remain materially different between FRESH and HISTORY; DXOLD also differs, while both arms report MODFLOW convergence.
NPF SAT differs as well, so the preregistered formal classification is MIXED_OR_UNRESOLVED rather than a solver-only classification.

The NPF SAT difference is consistent with the different current head, while the DBD arrays are source-defined history carriers. This localizes a concrete causal candidate but does not prove that resetting or disabling DBD would remove the path effect.
STO state, NPF conductance/static fields and accepted XOLD remain equal in this fixture.
No MODFLOW state was modified by the forensic diagnostic and no reset, convergence-rule change or production coupling policy is admitted.
next_natural_unit: Preregister a paired causal-isolation diagnostic that repeats the G21B FRESH/HISTORY experiment with the same physical model and response sequence but with delta-bar-delta under-relaxation disabled from solver initialization. Compare the standard DBD arm pair with the no-under-relaxation arm pair without mutating state mid-solve or altering any existing G21 evidence.
